title: 1Password Business to self-hosted Passbolt
summary: Passbolt is built for teams rather than families, with real access control. It is also considerably more work than Vaultwarden.

you_lose: 1Password's security team, audits and bug bounty
Polished mobile apps; Passbolt's are functional rather than pleasant
Watchtower breach monitoring and account recovery
you_gain: OpenPGP end-to-end encryption with per-user keys, which is a genuinely different security model
Sharing and access control designed for organisations rather than households
AGPL-3.0, free seats, and no per-user charge at any size

caveats: A password vault is the worst thing to lose. If you will not keep backups tested and the host patched, stay on 1Password whatever this page says.
Passbolt's key model means a lost private key is unrecoverable by design. That is a security feature and an operational hazard; plan recovery before you migrate.
It needs GPG, a mail server for invitations, and TLS. The 10-hour estimate assumes all three go smoothly, which they often do not.
